title: ProviderObservation
description: One value of one series at one period under one revision, AS THE PROVIDER REPORTED IT: the raw landing row that normalization reads from, kept so any canonical value can be traced back to the exact upstream reading. A DIRECT CONTRACT FOR data.observation (series_id, period, observed_at, value, revision, vintage, source, provider, provider_record_id, retrieved_at) with PK (series_id, period, observed_at, revision). The `revision` column is the point: a series whose provider restates history keeps BOTH the superseded and the restated row rather than overwriting, which is what makes a backtest honest. This is the plan §3/§6 provenance layer and it is DELIBERATELY NOT canonical data - plan §12 forbids storing provider JSON as canonical, so this row is a raw observation with bounded retention, not a domain entity.

provider.description: Which upstream this row came from. Matches data.observation.provider.

dataset.description: The provider's dataset within the source, when it has more than one.

series_id.description: The canonical series this reading belongs to (data.observation.series_id), NOT the provider's series name - the provider's spelling lives in provider_record_id.

period.description: The provider's OWN period label ('2026-09', '2026-10-09'), kept verbatim; observed_at carries the same period as a timestamp for windowing, so neither is derived from the other at read time.

observed_at.description: Part of the PK. The period as a timestamp, matching data.observation.

revision.description: data.observation.revision, defaulting to 'latest'. A restatement writes a NEW row under a new revision; it never overwrites the superseded one.

vintage.description: When the provider published this revision, distinct from observed_at (when we read it).
